text:
Seattle won on the scoreboard, but Philadelphia played the better game, and the shootout only confirmed how thin the margin was. Bobby McMann scored the power-play goal that opened the night and then buried the shootout attempt that ended it, which is why he took first star. Philadelphia had the better of the chances, 3.13 expected goals to 2.87, and deserved to win in 55 percent of simulated replays of every shot.

The first two periods belonged to the Flyers by quality and to the Kraken by finish. PHI outchanced SEA 1.45 to 0.76 in the second, yet Ville Ottavainen's snap shot, a 6 percent chance, made it 2-0 at 8:54. Philipp Grubauer then did the rest, stopping 24 of 26 and saving about 1.1 goals more than an average goalie would have faced with those shots. Dan Vladar was solid at the other end, 31 shots against and 0.87 goals saved above expected, but he could not make up the early gap.

Philadelphia answered in 73 seconds of the third. Christian Dvorak scored at 6:07, and Trevor Zegras tied it at 7:20 on a 20 percent chance, his fifth shot of the night. Overtime was all Seattle, 0.86 expected goals to none, and the Kraken had to lean on Grubauer to get through it. In the shootout, Matvei Michkov's goal was the only one for the Flyers, and McMann's deciding goal in the fifth round settled it.
